runs.name: Otis Worldwide Corporation
runs.entry: Price **$65.95** (close 2026-10-09, aggregator, flagged) x **380,669,339 shares** (10-Q cover as of 2026-07-15; issued less treasury agrees) = cap **$25,105M**; sovereign **5.60%**. Q1 IN (Service understood, 85% of five-year segment operating profit; New Equipment volume, China down more than 20% in each of 2024 and 2025, not foreseeable and not deciding) · Q2 IN (Service: price passed through every year of the inflation, units up 4% or more a year for four years, segment returns held through the cycle; the independents' half of the units recorded against it; New Equipment open, to Q7 at no growth) · Q3 for (customers fund the working capital; the minority buyouts earned under the floor, Zardoya at most about 4.6% after tax) · Q4 weighs against, no STOP (restructuring recurs every year and is left out of the featured figures; counted as cash) · Q5 integrity IN (the 2007 EU cartel fine under UTC recorded; misses reported and paid for), ability for, succession open (the chief executive leaves by July 2027) · Q6 against (a fixed-sum buyback with no stated price; Zardoya $1,802M debt-financed under the floor; pay on adjusted figures with no capital charge) · **Q7 OUT: owner cash $1,368M a year all-equity (2021 to 2025, bolt-ons deducted, minority buyouts left in net debt, a convention of the run), growth -0.58%; range $41.24 to $44.13 all-equity (net debt $7,623M; $52.14 to $58.56 equity-only), width 1.07 to one; fair price $15.20 ($31.21 equity-only); the price needs 3.69% growth for ten years just to earn the 5.60% Treasury.** Run by the interactive session's batch 9, killed by the session limit after the run's closing commit (258053ed) and before the fold; folded by the overnight cycle without a dispatch. The dispatcher re-checked: check_framework PASS; the analyst's check_quotes.py 75 ids, 28 fragments, 0 problems; the dispatcher's own fold_verify.py (straight and curly quotes) 17 fragments, 0 problems; no tracked research file over 200 KB. Departure owned in the self-audit: Q2, Q3 and Q4 committed together (dda8afda). Framework points for the operator (from the run): whether a minority buyout under specific (c) is deducted as capital spending or left in net debt (about $20 a share apart here); the tax on the interest added back on the all-equity basis (25% used, a convention); a segment measure restated inside the window; the fair-price midpoint of values or of growth (the gaps case's A). Brief errors: Carrier and Johnson Controls file no service-line margin; Hitachi filed 20-Fs to FY2010; the brief's Service test read segment profit where the framework says company operating profit (85% and 97%, the same answer). Position note filled at the fold: not held. Alert `OTIS-v5-fair` at $15.20; the v4.1 bands retired.
runs.narr: A maintenance franchise whose price held through the inflation, carrying $7.6bn of net debt from the spin and the minority buyouts, with owner cash flat to falling since 2021; priced well above a narrow range. Against: New Equipment in China shrinking, recurring restructuring left out of the featured figures, buyouts that earn under the floor, and an unnamed successor to the chief executive.
runs.fair_label: OTIS at/below $15.20: the fair price on the all-equity basis of the blind v5 purchase run of 2026-10-10 (Test Runs/2026-10-10 Run - OTIS Otis Worldwide.md; OUT at Q7 at $65.95; $31.21 equity-only). A prompt to re-run Q7, never a verdict.
